value.name: Marcus warns Asha about emotional involvement
value.description: Marcus tells Asha she is not the family's friend and warns her that she is getting too personally attached to the people in the case.
evidence: "I am not saying this to reprimand you. I am saying this because I have watched you for three years and I have seen you do this work better than anyone I know and I have also seen the cases where you came close to mistaking the people for the work, and this one has all the markings."

value.name: Marcus identifies warning signs in the case
value.description: Marcus points to specific family dynamics that make Asha vulnerable to overidentifying with the clients and making decisions for them.
evidence: "The daughter who looks at you a certain way. The housekeeper who has decided to trust you. The son who has, against the odds, started to behave. You like them. You like that they are starting to behave because of something you did. That is the dangerous part. That is the part where lawyers begin to make decisions on behalf of clients instead of for clients."

value.name: Asha denies acting for clients
value.description: Asha insists that she has not made any decisions on the family's behalf.
evidence: "I have not made any decisions on their behalf."

value.name: Marcus softens warning and ends call
value.description: Marcus clarifies that he is only cautioning Asha before the situation becomes irreversible, then jokingly asks her to buy him lunch and the call ends with a Tuesday lunch plan.
evidence: "I know you have not. I am saying that the conditions for it exist. I am saying it now while it is still possible to say it."
"Do not thank me. Buy me lunch."
"I will buy you lunch on Friday of next week. After Monday."

value.name: Asha records Marcus's warning
value.description: After hanging up, Asha sits with the receiver and adds Marcus's lunch reminder and warning to her yellow pad notes.
evidence: She hung up and sat for some time with her hand on the receiver, and then she picked up the yellow pad and wrote, beneath the items already there, an eighth item: "Marcus — Tuesday lunch — listen."

value.name: Asha continues her workday
value.description: The scene shifts into a routine workday as Asha handles the guardianship matter, writes a memo, and begins intake calls.
